passage:
Vinita: hey, you weren't at the bus stop. everything ok?
Tejas: yeah. Mum's shop closed down, so I walk now, it's fine
Vinita: oh. I'm sorry Tejas
Tejas: don't make it a thing pls 🙂
Vinita: I won't. Can I ask something small? I'm doing chemistry notes tonight, want to do them together? I'll come to the library
Tejas: you don't have to
Vinita: I want to. I'm also terrible at balancing equations 😅 you'd be doing me a favour
Tejas: haha ok. 5pm?
Vinita: 5pm. I'll bring the good biscuits. And I won't tell anyone, promise
Tejas: thanks Vinita ❤️

qa.q: Where will Vinita and Tejas study together?
Why did Vinita say they were terrible at balancing equations, and what did Vinita want?
qa.a: Vinita felt sorry for Tejas and wanted to help without making it a charity case, so Vinita framed the offer as Tejas doing Vinita a favour.

qa.q: What did Vinita do that helps Tejas, and what should Vinita avoid?
qa.a: Vinita offered time, notes and company and promised privacy. Vinita should avoid gossiping about the trouble in Tejas's family.

qa.q: How might Tejas feel about Vinita's offer?
qa.a: Grateful and a little relieved. Tejas first said Vinita didn't have to, then agreed and sent thanks with a heart, so the tone made it easy to accept.

grounding: A friend wants to help a struggling family by offering time and notes without making the friend a charity case.

passage:
After the hailstorm flattened the wheat, everyone in Dhanaura knew Chaitanya's family had lost almost everything. He came to school in the same shirt every day and stopped playing kabaddi after class. He went straight home to help his father clear the fields.
Rehana noticed he'd stopped submitting homework. She didn't bring it up in front of anyone.
Instead, at recess, she slid her notebook across. "I copied the maths notes twice by mistake. You want one?"
He looked at her carefully. "By mistake?"
"Totally by mistake." She kept her face straight.
In the afternoons she walked the longer path, past his field, and sometimes stopped to help him stack the broken stalks while they talked about cricket.
When a girl at the hand pump asked, "Is it true they can't even pay the school fees now?" Rehana just said, "Ask him yourself if you care," and walked on.

qa.q: How does Rehana feel about Chaitanya's situation?
qa.a: She feels caring and sympathetic, wanting to help him without making him feel like a charity case.

qa.q: How did Rehana help without embarrassing Chaitanya?
qa.a: She gave him notes with a light excuse, kept him company while he worked, and refused to gossip about his family.

qa.q: How might Chaitanya see Rehana's 'mistake' with the notes?
qa.a: Chaitanya seems to see through it but accepts the notes, probably relieved that she helps him quietly.

grounding: A teen helps a friend whose family is struggling by offering notes and company quietly, and refuses to gossip about them.

passage:
Yara's father had lost his job in the spring, and since then things had changed at her Copenhagen flat. Emil noticed small things: she skipped the class café trips, and her winter jacket was her brother's old one.
He didn't ask her about money. That felt like it would make her shrink.
Instead, on Tuesday, he said, "I'm terrible at chemistry. Want to study at the library after school? My mum packs too many sandwiches anyway."
Yara hesitated, then said, "Okay. But I'm not great either."
They studied three evenings a week. He shared the sandwiches, and she explained balancing equations far better than their teacher.
When a boy in class said, "Heard Yara's family is broke," Emil said flatly, "That's her business, not yours." The boy shrugged and dropped it.
On Friday, Yara said, "You know, this is the best part of my week." Emil grinned. "Mine too."

qa.q: What did Yara wear that was her brother's old one?
How does Emil feel about Yara's situation?
qa.a: He feels caring and protective, and worried that asking about money would make her feel ashamed.

qa.q: Which choices made Emil's help respectful?
qa.a: He offered study time and shared sandwiches casually, and he shut down the gossip instead of joining it.

qa.q: How does Yara seem to feel about their library evenings?
qa.a: Yara feels happy and valued, calling them the best part of her week, and she gets to help Emil too.

grounding: A teen helps a friend whose family is struggling by offering time, company and study help without making her a charity case or gossiping.
